titulo: Does setting the AC to 60 cool your house faster?
fuentes: U.S. Department of Energy (Energy Saver, thermostats): setting the thermostat colder than normal when you turn on the A/C will not cool the home any faster and could result in excessive cooling and unnecessary expense

frases.texto: You walk into a hot house and set the AC to sixty, so it cools off faster.
frases.estilo: Casual, like catching you in the act.

frases.texto: That's a myth. Sixty won't cool your house any faster than a normal setting.
frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: A thermostat isn't a gas pedal. It's a destination.
A basic air conditioner runs at one speed, no matter how low you set it.
All it does is keep running past the temperature you wanted.
The U.S. Department of Energy says setting it colder than normal won't cool your home any faster, and could mean excessive cooling and unnecessary expense.
Heads up: if a window is open or the sun is blasting in, no number will get you there.
Set it to a normal, comfortable temperature, and close the blinds.
Send this to the friend who sets the AC to sixty and waits.
frases.estilo: Playful, with humor, rhymes with the start.
